units.title: Canonical Transformations, Hamilton-Jacobi Equations, and Action-Angle Variables
Chaos
units.note: no college topic: nonlinear dynamics and chaos

units.title: Problem Set 1
examples: two gravitating masses in a uniform field: Lagrangian in CM and relative coordinates, Hamiltonian
double pendulum: Lagrangian, equations of motion, Hamiltonian
point mass on a rotating hoop (generalized coordinates)
two masses joined by a spring on a plane: Lagrangian and conserved quantities
Hamilton's principle for a Lagrangian with second derivatives (higher-order EOM)

units.title: Problem Set 2
examples: spherical pendulum in a viscous fluid: Rayleigh dissipation function and EOM
bead on a helix: constraint torque, energy and angular momentum
hoop rolling on a cylinder: Lagrange multipliers and the leaving angle
infinite rope over two pulleys: equilibrium shape (variational)
falling ladder against a smooth wall: constraint forces and separation angle

units.title: Problem Set 3
examples: rotation angle in Euler's theorem from eigenvectors of a rotation matrix
Foucault pendulum and the Coriolis force in a rotating frame
angular velocity components in terms of Euler angles
disk with a point mass on its edge: inertia tensor, principal axes, free rotation
cone rolling on its side without slipping: angular velocity and kinetic energy

units.title: Problem Set 4
examples: heavy symmetric top: steady precession rates
three masses on a circle with an exponential potential: normal modes
small oscillations of the double pendulum: normal modes for given masses
rigid bar on two springs: coupled translation–rotation modes

units.title: Problem Set 5
examples: canonical transformations and generating functions
canonical transformation for the harmonic oscillator
Poisson brackets and conserved quantities of a two-degree Hamiltonian
angular momentum and the Laplace–Runge–Lenz vector via Poisson brackets
motion in an exponential potential from Hamilton's equations
projectile by the Hamilton–Jacobi method

units.title: Problem Set 6
examples: charged particle in a plane with a magnetic field and a central potential: Hamilton–Jacobi
time-dependent linear potential: Hamilton–Jacobi solution
action–angle variables for V = F|x|: period
action–angle variables for V = a csc²(x/x₀)
3-D anisotropic oscillator in action–angle variables

units.title: Problem Set 7
examples: canonical perturbation theory for a mass between two springs
second-order perturbation theory for the pendulum
